target_customer: Enterprise engineering and security teams that want automated code vulnerability discovery and patching
problem: AI lets attackers find and exploit bugs faster than rule-based tools and manual audits can keep up, so defenders need autonomous vulnerability finding, proof of concept generation and patches.
business_model: Enterprise security software with services (audits, incident response); pricing not stated, demo-led sales
product_category: AI cybersecurity, autonomous code security agent (VEGA)

founders.name: Eten Zou
founders.background_notes: Pwn2Own win per the YC launch post. Self-reported.

founders.name: Yuan Tan
founders.background_notes: DARPA-funded program analysis research, Black Hat USA speaker.

founders.name: Frank Wu
founders.background_notes: DEF CON finalist with r3kapig, led a DARPA AIxCC repair team.

founders.name: Xiaochuan Yu
founders.background_notes: DEF CON finalist three years running.

competitors.name: XBOW
competitors.what: Autonomous offensive security platform that finds and validates vulnerabilities
competitors.traction_then: Reached top ranks on HackerOne earlier
competitors.funding_then: $120M Series C in March 2026 at over $1B valuation

competitors.name: depthfirst
competitors.what: Applied AI security lab, also published nginx RCE research

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous vulnerability research with working exploit and patch generation is research-grade, backed by claimed first public exploits for Android 17 and nginx.

defensibility.rationale: Elite founder expertise and a record of zero-days are hard to copy, but well funded rivals exist and model capabilities spread quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As of 2026 well funded autonomous security startups already occupied the wedge. No incumbent action against NebuSec found.

market_need_then: In 2026 AI accelerated both code generation and attacker vulnerability discovery. Funding rounds for XBOW and depthfirst show strong demand for autonomous security.

branding.domain_note: Uses nebusec.ai. YC lists the company as Nebula Security, so two names are in use.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and punchy, defender-side: The power dynamic just shifted back to the defenders.

branding.brand_signature: Audited by NebuSec as a mark of credibility from the number one hacking team
branding.community_and_virality: Self-published research (IonStack, GhostLock, nginx exploits) is the main visibility. No independent press about the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong founder credibility claims but a new brand, with two names in circulation and no independent coverage.

outcome_analysis: NebuSec is a few months old and active. It joined YC in Summer 2026 with a four person team of top CTF and DEF CON researchers and a code security product available now. Funding and customers are unverified, so no outcome story exists yet.
notes: Unverified funding: the company website alone claims a $7M seed with Llama Venture, Depth Venture and Y Combinator; a cross-check search found no such round for NebuSec (the matching $7M seed belongs to Capsule Security). Dealroom lists a $125K entry. None recorded as rounds. Bounty totals differ on company pages ($400K+ and $580K+ Google VRP). All founder achievements and the first exploit claims are self-reported. The firm is Nebula Security on YC and NebuSec on the website.
